review_policy: reviewed means every capture cited for the operation replays against the node with no difference, or with differences that only the deliberate gaps the operation lists account for, and at least one is cited, for the cases those captures cover; it never means exhaustive equivalence. known_gap names a difference a replay observes, and the capture's replay lists it exactly. not_reviewed means the cited captures, if any, don't settle the operation, even if the node routes it.

timestamped-signatures-only.text: Every signed operation: upstream also accepts a request whose auth chain signs only its method and its path below /v1 (lowercased), whatever x-identity-timestamp or x-identity-metadata header the request carries or omits, valid until the delegated key expires. The node accepts only the timestamped payload over its own method and path, at most five minutes old and one minute ahead, and refuses such a request with upstream's 401 {ok:false, data:{message}, error:'Unauthenticated'}.

signature-window.text: Every signed operation: upstream accepts a timestamp up to 30 minutes old or ahead; the node accepts at most five minutes old and one minute ahead, and refuses the rest with the same 401.

unauthenticated-message.text: Every signed operation: when a signature does not verify, upstream's data.message is its verifier's own text, which includes the payload it expected and its local clock; the node's is a fixed text naming the failed check (Invalid auth chain, Invalid timestamp, Expired signature, Invalid signature). The status, error and envelope are upstream's, and no client reads data.message.

chain-copy-lag.text: Every operation that reads a collection's published or approved state: upstream asks the Polygon collections subgraph on each request; the node reads its copy of that subgraph, which the shop's collections mirror refreshes every three times MARKETPLACE_MIRROR_INTERVAL_SECS (15 minutes at the default 300). A collection deployed outside the node's own publication flow reads as unpublished, and an approval or a role change as not made, until the next pass, so a client that polls after a deployment (the old builder web retries its publish every 5 seconds) waits up to that bound plus the subgraph's lag. When the copy has no complete pass the node answers 503, and when its last pass, or the row or absence a decision reads, is more than 30 minutes old it answers 503 to every request that grants access or writes. A standard collection deployed outside the node's own publication flow within that window still reads as a draft, so its owner can save it: a save that changes its name or calldata gives the row another computed address, and the row no longer maps to the deployed contract. Upstream refuses such a save by asking the Polygon RPC whether the stored address holds a contract, and by the day-long lock the old builder sets right after its deployment.

owner-is-the-chain-creator.text: Every operation that decides by a standard collection's owner: once the node's copy of the Polygon collections subgraph holds the collection, its owner is the chain creator for every check; before, the stored eth_address. Upstream compares the stored eth_address in some checks and the chain creator in others until an owner sync rewrites the row, so between a creator transfer and that sync a client of upstream sees the previous creator keep, and the new creator lack, part of the owner's access; the node gives all of it to the chain creator at once.

managers-from-chain-only.text: Every operation that admits an on-chain manager or answers a collection's managers and minters: the node reads managers and minters only from its copy of the Polygon collections subgraph, so only a collection on chain has them, and a PUT /v1/collections/:id body never sets them. Upstream also stores the managers and minters such a body carries for a collection that is not on chain, answers them and admits those managers.

access-checks-never-write.text: DELETE /v1/items/:id and POST /v1/items/:id/files: the node's access check changes no row. Upstream's can set a collection's stored eth_address, and its items', to the chain creator when they differ, so a later read of those rows names the creator.

access-before-kind-conflict.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id on an existing collection: the node answers 401 Unauthorized to upsert collection before it compares the body's URN with the stored collection, so only a signer who may save the collection gets the 409s for converting it or changing its third party. Upstream answers those 409s first.

committee-cache.text: GET /v1/committee: the node answers from the same read of the Polygon collections subgraph its committee decisions use, kept one hour, so a member added or removed shows up to an hour later. Upstream reads the subgraph on every GET /v1/committee and keeps its own read an hour for decisions.

committee-unavailable.text: Every operation a committee member may perform: when the Polygon collections subgraph can't answer, the node answers 503 to GET /v1/committee and to every decision only the committee could grant, and asks again after 30 seconds. Once its read is more than an hour old and a refresh has failed, a committee member reads published content as any signer does until a read succeeds. Upstream answers GET /v1/committee with an empty list and treats nobody as a member.

collection-list-bounds.text: GET /v1/collections and GET /v1/:address/collections: the node answers at most 1,000 rows (the committee's listing and the public search) or 5,000 rows (an address's own listing) per response, with or without page and limit, and a page's limit above that is answered with the cap as its limit. It refuses with 400 a q longer than 256 characters, more than 5 tag values, a tag longer than 64 characters, a repeated page, limit, q, sort, type or is_published, a type other than standard or third_party, and a negative page or limit, and matches q literally, % and _ included. Upstream answers every matching row, reads % and _ in q as wildcards, and answers those inputs otherwise.

address-listing-transferred.text: GET /v1/:address/collections: a collection whose stored owner is the address but whose chain copy names another creator and neither the address as manager or minter is left out of the results, of total and of the status counts. Upstream leaves it out of the results only, after paging, so its total and counts include it, the page that held it answers one row fewer and each later page starts one row further on than the node's.

collection-save-input.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id: the node refuses with 400 Invalid request body a body key the schema doesn't name, a blank name, a urn that is not a whole collection URN, a string field over 256 characters, a managers or minters list over 1,000 entries and data over 1 MiB. Upstream drops keys its schema doesn't name, accepts those values.

initialize-data-creator.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id for a standard collection: the node computes the contract address only from data that is initialize calldata naming the signer as the collection's creator, and refuses other data with 409 Cannot upsert a collection without a valid data, after it has checked who may save the collection. Upstream computes the address from any data string.

invalid-body-detail.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id with a body the schema refuses: both answer 400 {ok:false, data, error:'Invalid request body'}; upstream's data lists its JSON schema validator's errors, the node's is {}.

admin-addresses-not-admitted.text: GET /v1/collections/:id: upstream answers its ADMIN_ADDRESSES wallets the full body of a published collection; the node gives BUILDER_ADMIN_ADDRESSES no role on collection reads, and answers those wallets as any other signer.

polygon-mainnet-collections.text: GET and PUT /v1/collections/:id and both listings: the node computes a standard collection's address with the Polygon mainnet collection factory and answers urn:decentraland:matic: collection URNs. Upstream deployed against a test network (CHAIN_NAME Sepolia) uses the Amoy factory and amoy URNs.

stored-name-trimmed.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id: the node stores and answers a collection's name trimmed of surrounding spaces; upstream stores it as sent and answers it so, also in a refusal's data.

query-never-overrides.text: GET /v1/:address/collections and GET and PUT /v1/collections/:id: the node takes the address and the id from the path, and a PUT's collection and data from its JSON body, whatever the query string carries; upstream reads an address, id, collection or data query parameter before the path or body. No client sends one: the old builder web, the marketplace and this repository's clients put only the listing filters in the query string.

third-party-registry.text: The node reads no third-party registry: it takes the wallet stored as a third-party collection's creator as its provider's only manager, lets any signer create a third-party collection under any provider id, and answers is_programmatic false on a third-party collection's reads and address-listing rows and leaves it out of the committee's listing. Upstream reads the registry's providers and managers: a non-manager's create under a listed provider answers 401, every manager the registry lists reads, lists and saves its provider's collections, and is_programmatic is the provider's, also on the committee's listing.
third-party-registry.closes: The node reads the third-party registry's providers, their managers and whether each is programmatic, decides a third-party collection's managers and is_programmatic from it, and refuses a create under a listed provider by a wallet that doesn't manage it.

item-chain-merge.text: A published item's body is the node's own row: upstream merges the collections subgraph's item into it (urn, price, beneficiary, rarity and content_hash from the chain, is_published true).
item-chain-merge.closes: The node merges the chain copy's item into a published item's body as it merges a collection's.

item-curation-publicity.text: A third-party item with an item curation is not public on the node, which keeps no item curations; upstream answers any signer its public item.
item-curation-publicity.closes: The node keeps item curations and answers a curated third-party item publicly.

admin-addresses-items.text: The node gives BUILDER_ADMIN_ADDRESSES no role on item reads; upstream's ADMIN_ADDRESSES wallets read any published item in full.
admin-addresses-items.closes: The node admits its admin wallets to item reads as upstream admits ADMIN_ADDRESSES, or records the difference as deliberate.

item-list-fields.text: Item lists answer an empty description as "" where upstream answers null, and omit video when it is null.
item-list-fields.closes: The node answers an item list's description and video as upstream does.

minter-item-list.text: A minter of a collection on chain lists its minted items only; upstream lists every item, drafts included.
minter-item-list.closes: The node lists every item to a minter of a collection on chain.

status-before-existence.text: The collection items listing refuses an invalid status before it looks the collection up; upstream answers 404 for a missing collection first.
status-before-existence.closes: The node looks the collection up before it validates the status filter.

published-item-edits.text: The node answers 409 to every item save in a published collection; upstream lets the owner and an on-chain manager save an existing item's metadata and contents there.
published-item-edits.closes: The node accepts the owner's and an on-chain manager's metadata and contents saves of an existing item in a published collection, refusing a rarity change, a move or a new item.

lock.text: The node keeps no lock: it answers 423 while its own publication of the collection runs; upstream answers 423 while the collection's lock is under a day old.
lock.closes: The node keeps a collection's lock and answers 423 while it is under a day old.

item-urn-path.text: PUT /v1/items takes a UUID only and third-party item saves carry no URN; upstream also takes a third-party item URN in place of the id.
item-urn-path.closes: The node takes a third-party item URN in the path and saves third-party items by URN.

item-delete-body.text: DELETE /v1/items answers {id}; upstream answers data true.

published-item-uploads.text: The node answers 409 to uploads once the collection is published and 423 while its own publication runs; upstream accepts uploads from the owner, an on-chain manager or the provider's manager whatever the collection's state.
published-item-uploads.closes: The node accepts those uploads as upstream does.

item-files-body.text: POST /v1/items/:id/files answers the stored file map; upstream answers no data.

item-files-bounds.text: The node accepts at most 100 files and 20 MB together per upload; upstream bounds each file at 25 MiB and not their count.
item-files-bounds.closes: The node bounds uploads as upstream does, or records the bound as deliberate.
